title: Retry Policy Toolkit for an LLM Gateway
instructions: Implement `TransportError`/`ProviderError`, `parse_retry_after`, `RetryPolicy.delay`, `is_retryable` and `retry_async` in `llm_retry.py`. Classification, timing and execution are separate units: full-jitter backoff with `Retry-After` as a floor, no retry for quota 429s or oversized hints, and `asyncio.CancelledError` must propagate. Sleep and randomness are injected, so no test really waits.

evidence.label: parse_retry_after handles seconds and HTTP dates, clamps negatives and rejects nan/inf/junk
ProviderError stores its fields and RetryPolicy is a frozen dataclass with the default limits
delay stays inside the full-jitter window [0, min(max_delay, base * 2**attempt)]
Retry-After is a lower bound for the delay, not a replacement
is_retryable accepts transport errors, 429 and 5xx, but not quota 429s or client errors
Retries transient failures, honours the hint, then returns the result
A quota-exhausted 429 fails after one attempt
A Retry-After above max_retry_after is re-raised without sleeping
Re-raises the last error after max_attempts with no final sleep
CancelledError is not swallowed, so an outer timeout still works
